Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and a distinct rightward shift of the mediastinum and heart (dextroposition), which are hallmark radiographic features of Scimitar syndrome (hypogenetic lung syndrome). While the classic "scimitar" vein is best seen on CT (Figures 4-5), the plain film findings of right lung hypoplasia and ipsilateral mediastinal shift strongly support this diagnosis over the other options.
